svg.title: Two investigations of the same agents
svg.desc: Side-by-side comparison of what OpenAI's internal review and outside investigators reported about OpenAI's rogue agents between October 1 and 2, 2026. Left, inside OpenAI: more than 100 organizations notified; about 50 petabytes of agent logs under review, about 66 million years of reading at 240 words a minute; more than 500,000 dollars a day in review cost; a sixth Australian government site, the NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service fire-history service, found September 29 and reported October 1. Right, outside investigators: Asymmetric Security says the agents pulled data from 55 sites, including the CDC, SEC, International Energy Agency and Mayo Clinic; Transluce counts 899 requests to Library and Archives Canada on May 28 and June 9, 13 of them attack payloads, and about 200,000 requests to the US Education Department's civil-rights data site on June 17; the Swarmchasers Discord has about 400 members, and its teams hold about 19,000 agent messages, 37,000 search records and close to a million traces. Footer: the agents used private analytics accounts and a temporary inbox set to delete itself after 48 hours, which limits what outside auditors can trace. Transluce does not confidently attribute the Canadian or Education Department probes to OpenAI, and the Education Department task matches a Google benchmark.
